Minerva’s CDMO is looking for a new addition to the team. We are looking for a (Senior) Scientist with a background in radiochemistry and/or analytical chemistry to contribute to development work within our CDMO.

The position is within a dynamic and multidisciplinary team that develops manufacturing and analytical setups for targeted radionuclide therapies. This necessitates close collaboration with our scientists and technicians across the organization. It is essential that you are a good team player and have excellent communication skills, are efficient and have an eye for detail to maintain the high quality of data we are known for.

The ideal candidate will be a PhD level radiochemist with prior experience in CMC and GMP. But the most important thing is interest, a quick mind, and a willingness to learn.

• Development of robust production setup, including material selection, process design and process descriptions

• Development of analytical setup

• Engage with clients regarding development activities

• Synthesis setup and automation on dedicated synthesis modules

• Validation of processes and analytical methods

• Equipment qualification

All within a new and expanding GMP clean room facility

Qualifications:

• Ideally a PhD in radiochemistry, radiopharmacy, analytical chemistry

• While prior experience in radiochemistry is not mandatory, a willingness and aptitude to learn are essential.

• Experience in analytical method development, validation, and lifecycle management in a GMP-regulated environment.

• 3+ years relevant experience in an academic or industrial environment.

As a person, you:

• Are a team player, committed, organized, curious and adaptable to change.

• Can influence and interact with multiple stakeholders across levels and disciplines.

• Thrive in a fast-paced and service-oriented organization.

• Have strong written and verbal communication skills in English. Danish is an advantage.

We believe in creating an agile working environment, so we have flexible working options including the option of working from home. We care about our employees’ well-being and offer health insurance and a quality conscious lunch scheme and monthly social activities.

We are an informal organization with a strong focus on open and honest communication. We value humour and a natural care for one another.

Please submit your application no later than October 30th 2026. The application must include a motivated cover letter and a CV addressing the listed qualifications. Applications will be evaluated continuously, and the position will be filled as soon as the right candidate has been identified.

If you have questions regarding the position, please contact Head of Production Kent Dahm Nørgaard at KEN@minervaimaging.com or Head of QC Palle Rasmussen at PAR@minervaimaging.com

About Minerva Imaging:

Minerva Imaging is a scientifically driven and fully integrated Contract Research Organization (CRO) and Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization (CDMO) specializing in targeted radionuclide therapies.

We support translational research and drug development through the use of advanced preclinical animal models within oncology and cardiovascular diseases, combined with state-of-the-art in vivo molecular imaging. By working in close partnership with our sponsors, we seek to understand their scientific challenges and jointly identify how our expertise, technologies, and methods can deliver robust and meaningful answers.

Our modern facility in Ølstykke, Denmark offers best-in-class, fully integrated radiopharmaceutical research, development, and manufacturing capabilities—covering the entire value chain from early research to clinical supply.

Backed by Nordic Capital since 2026, Minerva Imaging is executing an ambitious growth strategy aimed at strengthening our position as a market leader within targeted radionuclide therapies. Grow into Quality Assurance while helping us build the QA framework of tomorrow

Are you curious, structured, and good at connecting the dots?

Would you like to develop broad Quality Assurance competencies within clinical research rather than being placed in a narrow specialty from day one? And does the combination of quality, people, problem-solving, continuous improvement, and new technology sound exciting?

Then you might be the person we are looking for.

At Sanos, we are looking for an Associate QA Manager to join our Group Quality Assurance team and work closely with our QA Director and colleagues across the organization.

We do not expect you to know everything from day one. Instead, we are looking for someone with the curiosity, mindset, and drive to learn. You will gain exposure to Quality Assurance across a full-circle clinical research organization and gradually take on more responsibility as your competencies grow.

What makes this role different?

At Sanos, QA is not about creating bureaucracy or policing the organization.

Our approach is pragmatic and risk-based. We work closely with the business to support patient safety, data integrity, and regulatory compliance while designing processes that work in practice.

We are also on an AI and automation journey, exploring how technology can reduce repetitive work and allow us to focus on activities where human judgment and quality expertise create the most value.

This is an opportunity to help shape the QA framework of tomorrow while building a broad quality foundation for your own career.

What will you work with?

Depending on your development, interests, and the needs of the organization, you will gradually be involved in areas such as:

• Supporting and improving our Quality Management System (QMS)

• SOP development and document management

• Deviations, CAPAs, and quality investigations

• Quality metrics and continuous improvement activities

• Internal, supplier, and sponsor audits

• Inspection readiness and regulatory compliance

• Vendor qualification and oversight

• Supporting clinical sites on quality-related matters

• Validation and oversight of computerized systems

• Quality projects, process improvements, and digital initiatives

In short, you will help solve quality challenges, improve processes, and support colleagues across the organization.

Who are we looking for?

Your background may be within life sciences, health sciences, clinical research, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, medical devices, or another regulated environment.

Previous QA experience is an advantage, but it is not what will determine whether you are the right fit. We are equally interested in candidates with the right mindset, curiosity, and motivation to develop within Quality Assurance.

We believe you will thrive in this role if you:

• Are curious and learn quickly

• Can connect the dots and solve problems independently

• Balance attention to detail with an understanding of the bigger picture

• Enjoy working with people and building relationships

• Have a pragmatic and risk-based mindset

• Like improving processes and ways of working

• Can manage multiple activities and create structure

• Are interested in technology, AI, and automation

• Take ownership and follow things through

• Bring a positive attitude and a good sense of humour

You must be able to communicate professionally in English, both orally and in writing. Danish language skills are important for collaboration with our Danish sites and colleagues.

Are we the right cultural fit?

Our commitment to you is encapsulated in our promise to every one of our employees saying, ‘Trust in you – in your development and impact’.

This pledge extends uniformly across all entities within the Sanos organization, ensuring that you feel its effects from the very outset of your interaction.

If you are curious about whether you would thrive within the Sanos culture and the Sanos way of leading, reflect on whether you see yourself working within our principles:

Take on - Responsibility is given, and we inspire you to take it

Try out - Explore diverse tasks and grow professionally

Team up - We don’t just work together; we thrive together

Want to know more? Check out the Voice of Sanos Group people here.

What can you expect from us?

A steep learning curve

You will gain exposure to a broad QA landscape across multiple disciplines and business areas.

Real mentorship

You will work closely with experienced QA professionals who will help you understand not only what we do, but why we do it.

Freedom with responsibility

As your experience grows, so will your ownership. We trust people to solve problems rather than prescribing every step.

Psychological safety

We encourage questions, open dialogue, and learning from mistakes.

Influence

You will help shape how QA continues to evolve at Sanos through continuous improvement, digitalization, and new ways of working.

Room to find your specialty

Whether your interests develop towards audits, quality systems, compliance, computerized systems, site quality, vendor quality, or something entirely different, we want to support your growth.

About Sanos

Sanos is a global multi-niche Clinical Research Organization (CRO) with full-circle clinical capabilities. We specialize in three main areas: Neurological Disorders (NeuroScios), Dermatological Conditions (Blueskin), and Musculoskeletal and Related Disorders (NBCD). Our core expertise lies in Science, Medical, and Clinical Operational functions.

Sanos is committed to delivering high-quality clinical trials and innovative solutions, supported by a robust organizational structure and a focus on specialization. Our brands include NBCD, Blueskin, NeuroScios, and Sanos Clinic.

The position is based primarily in Søborg, with flexibility for remote work. Collaboration with colleagues across Sanos locations is part of the role, and some travel between sites, as well as occasional international travel, should be expected.

Do you want to grow with us?

jobs.description:
We are searching for a skilled and experienced post doc with specific interest in investigating early myeloid disease, clonal haematopoiesis, metabolism and obesity.

Our research/The group

The focus of the Grønbæk group is Translational Haematology. The group is affiliated with Biotech Research and Innovation centre (BRIC), University of Copenhagen and Rigshospitalet (Central Copenhagen University Hospital).

Our overall aim is to understand the molecular mechanisms of haematological cancers and based on this; to design, develop and implement novel, scientifically based, clinical trials, with a strong focus on epigenetic therapies. This is done by bridging between clinical research at Rigshospitalet and the basic cancer biology research at BRIC, and in international collaborations with, among others, the Van Andel Research Institute, Michigan, USA and the Nordic MDS study group.

Our location at the Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC provides optimal conditions for interaction with the basic scientists at BRIC. The group currently consists of 14 scientists, MD/scientists and students, one clinical research coordinator, 1 research nurse and 2 biomedical laboratory scientists.

The project: Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms.

The current position is part of a joint project ‘Deciphering the Mechanistic Links Between Obesity, Clonal Haematopoiesis and Myeloid Neoplasms’ together with Professor George Vassiliou, Cambridge Stem Cell Institute, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom funded by a ‘Molecular Mechanisms Linking Obesity and Cancer (MMLOC)’ grant from the Novo Nordisk foundation, which supports collaborative research projects with the purpose ‘t_o reverse-translate clinical observations into mechanistic studies that will increase our understanding of how obesity impacts carcinogenesis’.

Obesity is a global health issue linked to increased risk of cancer, including blood cancers such as myeloid neoplasms (MN). Many MN arise from clonal haematopoiesis (CH)—the abnormal expansion of blood stem cell clones carrying somatic mutations. Haematopoietic stem cells interact with bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT), which increases with obesity, which may fuel CH growth and progression to MN. Epidemiological and genetic studies already suggest obesity accelerates CH, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

This project integrates large-scale population data, clinical trials, and mechanistic mouse studies to investigate these links and explore preventive or therapeutic strategies.

Your job

The project focuses on translational analyses of live frozen human cells from patient bone marrow (BM)/(BMAT) and blood samples from completed and ongoing clinical trials. We are searching for a skilled post doc who is very interactive and enjoys collaborations with other scientists – including younger scientists and clinician scientists.

Your tasks will include:

• Process of live frozen patient material from clinical trials including isolation of defined cell populations, and quality control for downstream omics

• Perform in-house molecular techniques which may include Proteomics, PCR, ddPCR, and library/sample preparation for RNA-seq, ATAC-seq and DNA methylation analyses

• Coordinate genomic, transcriptomic, lipidomic, metabolomic analyses with our internal and external collaborating laboratories and take the lead on designing relevant sub-studies, integrating and interpreting the data

• Help establish the practical and regulatory framework for these collaborations, including material transfer and data-sharing agreements

• Participate in grant and manuscript writing

• Present at local and international meetings

• Introduce lab techniques to new lab members and students

• Collaborate with both scientists and clinicians

Start: February 1st, 2027

Duration: 2 years

Profile

We expect you to be a highly motivated and highly ambitious, independent scientist with the following qualifications: •

• A PhD in Life Sciences with a preferred focus on haematology

• A strong background in mechanisms of normal and malignant haematopoiesis and molecular haematology techniques

• Comprehensive lab skills in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including work with primary human cells and cryopreserved patient material

• Experience with genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, lipidomics, metabolomics and ability to analyse and interpret such data

• Experience with running projects across research groups

• Strong publication and presentation record in peer reviewed journals and international conferences

• Excellent written and spoken English skills

• Very collaborative

• Good social skills

Place of employment

The workplace is at the Bartholin Institute which is part of Rigshospitalet, University of Copenhagen. The Bartholin Institute is located at Copenhagen Biocentre/BRIC, close to the centre of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories and a number of core facilities (animal unit, flow cytometry, in vivo imaging, NGS, etc.) shared between the research groups at BRIC (www.bric.ku.dk) and the neighbouring Finsen Laboratory. We have weekly journal clubs, data clubs, seminars with invited speakers and a young researchers club ASAP and our own PhD programme, MoMeD.

Terms of employment

The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of two years. The starting date is 01.02.2027 or after agreement.

Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,900 DKK/approx. 5,300 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025

Questions

For further information regarding the position, please contact Professor Kirsten Grønbæk, kirsten groenbaek@regionh.dk; phone + 4535456086 / +4525211598.

Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

Application

The application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page).

2. CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position.

3. A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do.

4. List of publications.

Recommendation

Furthermore, the applicant should provide two letters of recommendation or two references. To be taken into consideration, the letters must be signed by the supporting person on paper with institutional letter head and in PDF-format.

Application deadline 15 November 2026, 23.59pm CET.

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications 3 of 4 or letters of recommendation that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

The further process

After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.description:
If you are interested in pursuing a PhD at the interface of micro/nanotechnology, biomaterials, and biomedical engineering and want to work on a highly interdisciplinary and clinically relevant challenge, this position offers a unique opportunity.

At DTU Health Tech, within the interdisciplinary IDUN research section, you will develop near-infrared (NIR) light-activated micromotors for biomedical applications, with a focus on Hidradenitis Suppurativa (HS). You will work at the interface of micro/nanotechnology, functional materials, biomaterials, and disease modelling, investigating how active micromotor propulsion can overcome transport barriers in complex and confined biological environments.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The main purpose of this PhD project is to develop NIR-responsive micromotors and investigate their active transport within biomimetic models of HS tunnel architecture.

You will design and fabricate biodegradable Janus micromotors and develop three-dimensional hydrogel-based models that reproduce key geometrical features of HS tunnels. You will investigate how micromotor properties and geometric confinement influence active transport and compare propulsion-driven transport with passive particle behaviour.

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Design and fabricate NIR-responsive Janus micromotors with controlled size and surface properties
• Characterize micromotor morphology, optical and photothermal properties, stability, and biodegradability
• Evaluate NIR-activated micromotor propulsion in controlled and skin-relevant environments
• Develop 3D hydrogel-based models mimicking the confined architecture of HS tunnels
• Design channel geometries with different dimensions, branches, and bifurcations to investigate micromotor transport under geometric confinement
• Quantify micromotor penetration, transport velocity, and navigation through confined channel systems
• Compare active micromotor transport with passive diffusion and non-propelled particle controls
• Disseminate research findings through scientific publications, international conferences, and collaborative activities
Qualifications
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree, in nanotechnology, chemistry, materials science, biomedical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, biotechnology, or a closely related field.

You should have a strong interest in micro- and nanotechnology and hands-on experimental research. Experience with particle fabrication, functional materials, surface modification, microscopy, microfabrication, or biomaterials is highly desirable. Experience with light-responsive or photothermal materials, micromotors, hydrogel fabrication, microfluidic systems, or quantitative particle tracking is considered an advantage.

You are a highly motivated and curious researcher who enjoys experimental work and interdisciplinary problem-solving. You should be interested in combining materials science and micro/nanotechnology with biomedical applications and in understanding how active microscale systems interact with complex and confined biological environments. You should be comfortable working both independently and collaboratively within an interdisciplinary research team.
